text:
alex_support: Customer opened a ticket—401 invalid_api_key after uploading a dashboard JSON. They say the same key works when pasted into curl locally.

alex_support: Pasted their uploaded JSON (redacted):
```json
{
  "name": "prod-integration",
  "credentials": {
    "service": "thirdparty",
    "token_blob": { "apiKey": "eyJhbGciOi..." }
  }
}
```

simon_support: Can you get the request-id from the customer's failing call? Also need org_id and which endpoint they hit (hosted/dedicated/private).

alex_support: Request-id: req_20240328_9abcef, org_id: org-5443, endpoint: hosted (api.redwood.com/v1/complete). Customer says they copied the key from our dashboard 'Upload' flow.

maria_engineer: Quick hypothesis: the dashboard uploader might have stored the whole nested object as the 'api key' string (base64 or JSON) instead of the raw token. If so the incoming Authorization header will be a JSON blob -> parsing fails as malformed key.

alex_support: Repro steps for us:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat bad_key.txt)" \
  -H "Redwood-Org: org-5443" \
  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/complete" -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

ops-bot: deploy-log:auth-service parsed token length=186 -> rejected malformed token

maria_engineer: I pulled the auth logs for req_20240328_9abcef — shows token contained leading "{\"apiKey\":\"" sequence and trailing "\"}\n" — definitely the uploaded JSON object string. Reason=malformed_api_key

simon_support: So customer copied the whole object from the dashboard JSON preview instead of the inner value. Can we craft a short reply to customer with exact fix steps?

alex_support: Drafting reply: "It looks like the dashboard upload saved a JSON object into the key field. Please open your dashboard export, copy the inner apiKey value only (no surrounding braces or quotes), and retry. You can verify by running:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "Redwood-Org: org-5443" https://api.redwood.com/v1/models/list
```
If you still see 401, paste the last 6 chars of the key and we will inspect logs."

maria_engineer: Also add: if the value looks like base64 of JSON (starts with "eyJ"), it was probably encoded—ask them to decode or copy raw. We can add a small server-side heuristic to reject keys that contain JSON brackets to improve UX.

simon_support: Sent to customer, they replied "that did it — I extracted the nested apiKey value and it's working now" :tada:

alex_support: Closing case-12345. Marking resolved. cc @maria_engineer for follow-up about uploader validation.

maria_engineer: Filing a small ticket to add validation and clearer copy in dashboard UI. Will attach logs and sample payload.

ops-bot: ticket-created: UI-1289 uploader:validation
